correctness.rationale: At p_*, the known triple has four norms equal 3/2 and three pair norms equal 2, yielding F=0; all arguments are nonzero and p_*>2 gives C² differentiability. Differentiating produces M_ij=P_u+δ_ijP_vi, with each P=I-vv^T/3. A reproduced exact rational characteristic-polynomial calculation gives t(t−1)^4(3t²−12t+4)^2/9; nullity one is exactly scaling. Spectral Taylor expansion combined with 1-homogeneity proves sharp coefficient (p_*-1)(1−√6/3)/2 and strict local rigidity. The positive restricted Hessian and a standard implicit-function theorem give the unique local minimizing branch, whose positive one-sided slope is 6 log3/p_*². Finite checks supplement the exact matrix identity and analytical argument.

value.rationale: The new endpoint conjecture is an explicitly motivated classification question. The canonical symmetric equality triple is the sharp documented supercritical obstruction. A computed full transverse spectrum and sharp Euclidean rigidity coefficient give substantive local geometric information about this natural obstruction. The one-sided parameter persistence excludes a fixed cone of possible witnesses immediately below the critical exponent, beyond verifying a numerical equality or a cheap sign check. The theorem is deliberately local and does not claim to resolve the global question.
